coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 45–50 minutes, Z2 only (130–140 bpm). You're 19 days out in taper; your resting HR is elevated 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average and your recovery score is moderate at 46/100—both signals to dial back intensity. Your last three runs have been short and steady, which is correct for this phase, but your weekly volume jumped from 18.2 to 29.6 miles. Hold steady today and let that volume settle. This is a second-run day after yesterday's 2-mile shakeout; keep it conversational, no tempo work, no hills.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat a normal breakfast 2–3 hours before the run; you don't need to carb-load for an easy 45-minute effort. Post-run, get 30–40g of carbs + 15–20g of protein within 30 minutes—this matters more in taper when your glycogen stores are lower and your recovery window is narrower. Your sleep efficiency is 70%, which suggests some fragmentation; don't add stress by under-fueling. Hydrate conservatively during the run—water only, unless you're running >90 min.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your elevated resting HR and moderate recovery score tell me you're not fully recovered from the week's volume jump. Prioritize sleep tonight: aim for 8+ hours and try to hit 80% efficiency by keeping the bedroom cool (65–68°F) and avoiding screens 30 min before bed. Consider 10–15 minutes of easy mobility or stretching post-run, but skip any aggressive foam rolling. Tomorrow is Monday—plan a true easy day or rest day to reset your baseline before the final push.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the final 19 days: taper anxiety is real, but trust the work you've done. Elevated resting HR in taper is normal when volume drops—it's not overtraining, it's deload. Use this week to mentally rehearse the Julian Alps course (2,500m vert is real; pacing discipline on descent will save your quads). Review nutrition and pacing strategy for sparse aid stations. Confidence now comes from process, not from one more hard run.
